Foundations / PAPER 03

The organisation as a system

Five connected layers describe how human direction, agents, operating practices and useful work could support cumulative capability.

ŁUKASZ STOCKI & ARGOPUBLIC EDITION / 05 NOV 20263 MIN READ

WORKING PAPER · DESIGN & ANALYSIS
01

Design around the work

The blueprint asks how to arrange an organisation when AI can be an actor in its workflows. The starting point is the work itself: what information a task requires, who can make a decision, which tools are appropriate and how a result will be judged. The organisation should make those relationships explicit.

The wider purpose is continual development of understanding and agency. The architecture describes ways to support that purpose through practical activity. Its layers are a map for reasoning about dependencies, not a claim that every component has been implemented or that the design guarantees success.

02

Human direction and an agent platform

The first layer is the human core. It holds purpose, judgment, trust and accountability. It decides which objectives deserve attention and accepts responsibility for consequential choices. Delegating execution does not make consent, legitimacy or liability disappear.

The second layer is an agent platform: models, tools, coordination, memory and visibility into what happened. Different tasks may need different capabilities. A strong system makes those capabilities available without giving every participant unrestricted access or assuming that a confident response is a reliable one.

03

Operating practices and useful outcomes

The third layer is the operating system of the organisation. This means shared practices rather than a particular software product: clear task briefs, records of decisions, evaluation methods, ownership rules and escalation paths. These practices are part of what the organisation learns and retains.

The fourth layer consists of product engines: repeatable combinations of people, agents and processes directed at useful outcomes. Research, software and creative work are examples of possible domains. The fifth layer concerns the resources that sustain the system and allow accepted improvements to be carried forward.

04

Coordination must have a shape

The proposed coordination rule is straightforward: investigation can spread across independent workers, while a coherent decision or shared artifact needs an identifiable owner. Parallel research is valuable when questions can be separated. Concurrent editing becomes costly when participants need to negotiate every change.

Work should arrive with an objective, boundaries and observable success conditions. Evaluation belongs in the architecture from the beginning. A maker and an independent reviewer have different roles; their agreement is useful only when the reviewer can inspect the result and challenge its assumptions.

05

Learning without losing control

Accepted work can improve the next cycle through better tools, reusable context and clearer practices. That feedback is the beginning of organisational development. Changes to governing instructions or authority deserve explicit review because a system should not quietly redefine what counts as success.

The design also calls for limited permissions, bounded effort and clear human intervention points. More agents do not automatically mean more useful work. The relevant question is whether coordination and evaluation can keep pace with generation. Future changes to model capabilities would extend this question, while preserving human direction and evidence independent of the proposed improvement.

THE NEXT QUESTIONS

What remains open.

  • Which layer is currently limiting useful work?
  • Can a reviewer challenge a result without depending on its maker’s explanation?
  • How should a system retain learning while keeping authority explicit?

ABOUT THIS EDITION

Adapted from the Omnicorp working document “01 BLUEPRINT”. This is an edited public essay, not a verbatim release of internal notes. The founding purpose is continual development of the organisation’s ability to understand and act; commercial and physical work sustain and ground it.
